summary: The previous redesign stack did not reach Settings, so it is still the old modal. WorkspaceSettings in web-next/src/components/workspace-settings.tsx opens as a backdrop dialog from the sidebar profile menu, with its own sidebar, an X button and a "Back to workspace" link. The boards show a full-page Settings section inside nx-main. It opens from the Rail's Settings button, has a "Settings · <org>" crumb header, and a left st-nav. Every page in the boards is built from st-group > st-card > st-row blocks, with switches, selects and chips. The code instead uses workspace-settings-section, -row and -form blocks with h3 titles and forms. The design adds two pages, "Your agent" and "Notifications". The code puts agent access, app updates, the answer guard and team call emails on Account and has no notification matrix. People, Teams and Billing are lists or forms in the code where the boards show tables or a plan card. Tool access, Slack and Email are only partly there: Slack is close, Tool access is a read-only rollup, and Email shows static "always sent" copy where the board has a forwarding address. Most of the restructuring works with existing routes. The notification matrix, quiet hours, answer style, custom masking categories, per-tool "who can use", email forwarding, Slack ask-display toggles, data region, retention, export, invoices, payment method and profile edit have no API, so they must be stubbed.

summary: The Library is far from the board. #240 only renamed the section, so knowledge-bases.tsx still shows a grid of knowledge-base cards that open a separate detail page (knowledge-base-detail.tsx) with forms and an Ask box. The board instead has one two-pane page: a Collections and Sources rail, search, a List/Grid toggle, an out-of-date note, Pinned tiles and a Recent table showing owner, tags and update time. Nothing in the Library opens a file: document rows only link out to external URLs. The one viewer in the app is PrimaryAgentFileViewer, which is reachable only from Agents. It has a back button, a badge, the name, Edit and Download over DocumentPreview, which has single-page PDF, docx, pptx-as-images, xlsx/csv tables, markdown and text, with no thumbnails, zoom, search, line numbers, video or code. Of the board's viewer features, these can be built in the browser today: thumbnails, zoom, page counter, find in page, sheet row/column headers and formula bar, slide filmstrip, image fit/zoom, line-numbered code, download and open original. Cited-passage highlights work only for text documents. Pinned, cited counts, out-of-date flags, comment pins, versions, recordings and transcripts, repo tree/blame/history, presence and Show in parley have no API.

summary: With #304–#306 counted as merged (feat/parley-room-chat is a superset of all three), the code has three parley surfaces: the strip on the teamspace page, the mini player and a full-page overlay (CallFullPage). The full page is fairly close to HuddleFull, and the device picker, room chat pane and ended dialog are all there. Three of the four parley boards are a different structure. HuddleShare, HuddleBrowse and HuddleMix put the parley in the main column, with the Rail and the agent panel still on screen. That view has a crumb header and a Full page pill, a shared screen with a column of named cams beside it, live browser tiles and a Mix tiling of people, the room, the screen and a browser. None of that exists today: call-surfaces.tsx has only pip and overlay modes, and live browsers are never shown inside a parley. The pop-ups are mostly missing. There is no shared pop-up primitive (only ui/dialog.tsx, used by the credential dialog), no welcome, invite, upgrade or hover card, no styled toasts (the Toaster is mounted but toast() is never called) and no modal delete; deletes are inline ConfirmStep groups. Several board elements need APIs that don't exist yet: parley notes and decisions, a list of past parleys, a member-started shared browser and driving, browser URL and title, members stopping an agent's browser, an org-wide "parley live" signal, agent access when inviting, and plan limits for parleys.

Edge: web-readable browser state GET …/browser/{id} {url, title, requestedBy, step} (LiveChild today has no url, title or requester)

Edge: POST …/call/signal {kind:'hand'|'reaction', value} broadcast to the call, only if RealtimeKit broadcastMessage isn't allowed by the member preset
Edge or Go: org-wide active calls read (which teamspaces have a live parley and who started it), for the 'started a parley' toast and the hover card's 'Parley live'
Go: per-teamspace setting 'let members' agents read this teamspace' and a teamspace share link, for the Invite dialog
Go billing: parley entitlements on the plan (max parley minutes, recordings allowed) and an edge refusal code when a limit is hit, to trigger the Upgrade dialog

slices.title: Run cards: the agent conversation as a working session
slices.delivers: Each member message becomes a task line (left-aligned, no bubble, small 'You · 09:41'). Under it, one run card on --canvas: a status pill (Working with Thinking Orb / Waiting for you / Done / Interrupted / Failed), elapsed time from item `at`, and Stop while running. Steps sit in an expandable list, one line per tool call with app mark, humanized name and key argument (query, file, URL, channel), and failed steps show their error. 'What it opened' is derived honestly from tool_call arguments. Approvals are inline blocking cards (existing ConfirmationCard). Outputs are file cards (FileKindBadge, name, vN, Open → right pane, Download) and request cards. The answer is markdown at the end of the card. The composer becomes a task bar with a 'Looking at …' chip from getScreenContext. This is visibly different from DM bubbles. Closes the working-session gap and the tool-row and composer differences.

GET /v1/organizations/{org}/agents/{agentID}/threads/{threadID}/artifacts/{name}: open a specialist's files like primary-thread artifacts
Members list (GET /v1/organizations/{org}/members) or a read-only endpoint: each member's primary agent {agent_id, name}, so People and DMs can show and ask anyone's agent without a shared teamspace

Member profile fields: timezone (for local time) and title/department
Agent stats: primary agent answered-today and files-made counts; per-specialist run count over the last 7 days; paused_by and paused_at on agents
